samples.question: This image shows three running lanes drawn on white paper, one above the other, separated by pale grey lane lines. Each lane holds exactly one RUNNER, a solid coloured disc, and exactly one FINISH POST, the short upright dark grey bar drawn in that same lane. The three runners are red, green and blue, and every finish post belongs only to the lane it is drawn in, so each runner is judged against the post in its own lane and never against a post in another lane. The GAP of a runner is the distance from the centre of that disc rightwards to the centre of the post in its own lane, measured across the page; every runner in this set is drawn to the left of its own post. The finish posts do not stand in a line: each post is placed in its own lane independently of the others, so the runner that is farthest to the right on the page need not be the runner with the smallest gap. Which runner has the smallest gap, which colour that runner is, how far to the right each runner sits, and the size of each disc are all chosen independently of each other, so no colour, position or disc size predicts the answer. The pale grey page frame, the two grey corner ticks and the grey lane lines are decoration and mark no finishing position. No image in this set is a borderline case: the smallest gap is at least 26 pixels smaller than the next smallest, and the rightmost runner sits at least 26 pixels right of the next one. Report what this picture in front of you actually shows, and do not answer from the usual assumption that the runner farthest ahead on the page must be the one closest to finishing. Which runner has the smallest gap to the finish post in its own lane? Answer exactly one of: red, green, blue.
